**STEP 1 - Scene:** A snack of whole almonds on a white square plate, photographed from directly above.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate is about 19 cm across, a side-plate size. Its area is roughly 330 cm² after allowing for the rounded corners.

**STEP 3 - Items:** Whole almonds only (about 30 pieces). No oil or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The almonds fill a cluster covering about 20% of the plate, roughly 65 cm².

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pile is about 1.2 cm high on average, so 65 cm² × 1.2 cm ≈ 78 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole nuts have a bulk density of about 0.5 g/ml, so 78 ml × 0.5 ≈ 39 g. Counting about 30 almonds at about 1.2 g each gives about 36 g, which agrees. I use 36 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw almonds are about 579 kcal/100 g, so 36 g × 5.79 ≈ 208 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 30 almonds is about 36 g and about 200 kcal, which is plausible for a small handful on a side plate.
